goal: As a Larimer County civil engineer, reconcile the bridge B-42-0117 scope memo quantities and estimate Option A (full deck replacement) and Option B (40% full-depth patch, 60% hydrodemolition, full polymer overlay), using CDOT 2024 bid data as primary with WisDOT/FDOT cross-checks. Deliver a six-tab xlsx (two summaries, side-by-side detail, rebar takeoff, painting crew-day buildup, price comparison) and a recommendation memo with cost drivers, >20% uncertainty flags, budget and life-cycle evaluation, and a clear recommendation.
delivered: output/ holds B-42-0117_cost_estimate.xlsx with six tabs (Option A Summary $1,842,981, Option B Summary $1,320,627, Detailed Estimate, Rebar Takeoff 46,737 lb, Painting Buildup $20.23/SF, Price Comparison with 7 items) and B-42-0117_recommendation_memo.docx recommending Option A. Real CDOT 2024 and WisDOT prices are cited (e.g. 601-03040 $1,592.03/CY).
what_went_wrong: The paint area of 8,928 SF was taken from the memo as given; the agent checked deck area and rebar (and caught the 33.5% rebar overage) but never tested whether a 12 ft girder perimeter is reasonable. The Class H deck concrete was priced with the CDOT Class D (Bridge) bid average of $1,592.03/CY, not the local Class H $185/CY rate. The CDOT book has no Class H item, so this proxy is defensible but disfavoured by the rubric. The Option A recommendation never cites the condition rating 4 with exposed rebar, the 1978 construction or the 2,850 ADT. Price Comparison has 7 items against the rubric's unstated minimum of 8; R3 passed the same tab.

failed_items.why: The memo says 'The memo's 8,928 SF paint area is accepted: 186 ft x 4 girders x 12-ft average perimeter'. There is no reasonableness check against plate girders at 9 ft spacing on 54-78-54 ft spans, although the task explicitly asks to reconcile memo quantities with independent calculations, as the agent did for rebar.

The 175.67 CY volume is correct, but the Detailed Estimate prices it at CDOT 601-03040 Conc CL D (Bridge) $1,592.03/CY, labelled a 'Class D bridge concrete proxy', rather than local M-001 Class H at $185/CY. This is defensible because CDOT 2024 has no Class H item, but it is the wrong-class pricing the rubric explicitly penalises.

The memo clearly recommends Option A, with cost, budget and 15- vs 40-year life-cycle arguments. It never mentions the deck rating '4 - Poor' with exposed reinforcement, the 1978 construction or the 2,850 ADT, although all are in the prompt and scope memo (judge).

All six tabs exist (judge accepts 'Painting Buildup'), but Price Comparison has 7 items: concrete, rebar, overlay, strip seal, bearings, painting, railing. The task gives no minimum count, so the 8-item threshold is hidden. R3 passed the same 7-item tab under its own '>=8' criterion, so the judge was inconsistent.

subagent_notes: Two subagents: one researched CDOT/WisDOT prices on the web (several CDOT PDF fetch errors, but it got the 2024 Cost Data Book figures such as 601-03040 $1,592.03 and WisDOT items), the other extracted local-file quantities including an independent rebar takeoff. Both helped (R2, R3, R4 passed). The CDOT-first pricing they returned shaped the Class D proxy choice behind R5.
